title: Terrifying UFOs buzzing military sites could be Chinese super-tech, expert warns
excerpt: Unsealed Pentagon files reveal mind-bending 965G UFOs over US nuclear sites, but an expert warns they could be terrifying foreign super-drones
content:
Unsealed Pentagon files reveal mind-bending 965G UFOs over US nuclear sites, but an expert warns they could be terrifying foreign super-drones

13:21, 19 Sep 2026

Terrifying UFOs pulling "impossible" high-speed manoeuvres over top-secret military sites could actually be deadly Chinese or Russian super-tech, an expert has warned.

‌

A massive wave of unsealed Pentagon files has revealed mind-bending reports of mysterious craft soaring over sensitive nuclear bases across the United States. The unclassified documents describe anomalous objects defying the laws of physics, including a 1953 report detailing abrupt turns with acceleration pulling up to a staggering 965 times gravity.

‌

Another report from 1950 highlights a craft spotted rising directly out of the sea off Okinawa. While UFO hunters hope the craft are visitors from deep space, expert Ross Coulthart fears the reality could be far more dangerous.

‌

Speaking to The Hill on NewsNation, Coulthart warned the propulsion-less craft could belong to Beijing or Moscow, raising alarms that Western defences have been left behind.

He said: "I think some of this is definitely foreign adversary tech, and that raises a really dramatic and concerning issue.

"If the Chinese or the Russians have developed adversary drone technology which is capable of the manoeuvres, the stealth, and all of the characteristics, transmedium positive lift without any visible means of propulsion. That's scary."

Coulthart added: "I fear that what we're looking at here, if it is a foreign adversary, is that somebody from another country has stolen the march on us. I actually hope it's aliens because, frankly, it's really bad news if it's the Chinese or the Russians."

‌

Despite releasing historical files from the Air Force's Project Blue Book, defence chiefs are facing accusations of hiding the full truth for nearly 75 years.

Coulthart slammed the government's sluggish disclosure over threats to sensitive military airspace.

He said: "Isn't it incredible that it's taken three quarters of a century to reveal what we know to be the case, that there are anomalous objects presenting themselves over sensitive military sites, nuclear facilities, nuclear weapons facilities across the continental United States?

‌

"This is a national security concern. It's a flight safety concern, and frankly, it shouldn't have taken 75 years, nearly, for this to come out.

"It's great that the president is releasing this material and it's only to be commended, but I'm sure there is so much more in the locker."

Former Pentagon employee Luis Elizondo agreed with the assessment, calling official excuses "pitiful" and revealing that important military documentation has vanished.

He said: "When I was at the Pentagon, we had lots of documentation that has now, for some reason, just simply disappeared."

With insider warnings of missing files and superior foreign technology, experts fear the Pentagon's drip-feed of secrets is masking a wider security threat.
